scenarios.description: Drive a POP command when buf_empty=1 and verify err_pulse asserts 1 cycle later while buf_count remains 0
Drive sequential PUSH commands to fill all 4 buffer entries from empty to full, verifying buf_count increments 0->1->2->3->4 and buf_full asserts
Drive SETOFF for Client 0 with offset 0, followed by READ, verifying resp_valid asserts 1 cycle later with the sample originally pushed
Drive concurrent req0 and req1 for consecutive clock cycles and verify gnt0 and gnt1 strictly alternate every clock cycle
Drive a PUSH when buf_full=1 and verify err_pulse asserts 1 cycle later while buf_count remains 4 and existing samples are preserved

requirements.description: Grant signals gnt0 and gnt1 must be evaluated combinationally within the request cycle based on req0, req1, and last_served.
A granted PUSH command (cmd=2'b01) appends data_in to tail and increments buf_count by 1 if buf_count < 4.
A granted POP command (cmd=2'b10) increments head by 1 and decrements buf_count by 1 if buf_count > 0.
A granted SETOFF command (cmd=2'b11) updates the requesting client's indirect offset register with data_in[1:0].
A granted READ command (cmd=2'b00) computes target address (head + client_offset) mod 4 and asserts resp_valid, resp_client, and resp_data 1 cycle later if client_offset < buf_count.
Attempting PUSH when buf_full=1, POP when buf_empty=1, or READ with client_offset >= buf_count leaves buffer state intact and asserts err_pulse for 1 cycle 1 cycle after the grant.
Clients initiate requests by asserting req0 or req1 along with cmd and data_in on posedge clk.
The DUT combinationally asserts gnt0 or gnt1 in the cycle of request if accepted by arbitration.
Unselected client request in contention receives gnt=0; the client must retain or reassert request in subsequent cycle if it desires service.
Read response pipeline returns data exactly 1 clock cycle after grant: resp_valid is a 1-cycle pulse.
resp_client identifies which client receives resp_data (0 for client 0, 1 for client 1).
Write commands (PUSH, POP, SETOFF) do not generate a read response on resp_valid.
Testbench verifies round-robin fairness under simultaneous dual-client request bursts without starvation
Circular buffer wrap-around pointer arithmetic correctly handles sample insertion and deletion beyond index 3
Read response pipeline correctly tags returning data with appropriate resp_client matching granted client
All invalid operations (push full, pop empty, unpopulated read) trigger err_pulse and preserve buffer integrity
